No experimental validation: all results are worst-case theoretical analysis without empirical studies of tightness or practical performance
Very long and complex impossibility proofs (Theorems 4.3, 4.4, 5.6) with extensive case analyses that are difficult to verify and lack intuitive explanation

Significant open problem left unresolved: whether EF1 is achievable for n≥3 with frequency predictions, creating a gap in the theoretical narrative
No robustness analysis for noisy/imperfect predictions despite claiming this is important for practice; limited discussion of how models apply practically

Novel algorithms that meaningfully extend prior work: Algorithm 1 achieves both EF1 and PROP1 with normalization information; Algorithm 2 cleverly leverages frequency predictions through picking sequences
Tight bounds (e.g., Theorem 6.3 with (√5-1)/2-EFX and matching impossibility) demonstrate technical precision
Complementary positive results and matching impossibilities across settings illuminate fundamental limits and enhance understanding

Adversarial constructions, while clever, follow similar structural patterns across multiple theorems, limiting technical novelty in this direction
